“research the history of tea”

Tea began in southwest China, where wild Camellia sinensis grew in the hills of Yunnan, and legend credits the emperor Shennong with a first cup around 2737 BCE, when leaves blew into his boiling water.

Whatever the truth of that story, by the Han dynasty tea was a medicine, and by the Tang it was a daily drink across China.
